findings.failure_path: the credential redaction anchors \b directly before (api[_-]?key|key|token|secret|password), so compound names with word-character prefixes — access_token=, refresh_token=, client_secret=, openai_api_key= — never match (no boundary after `_`), and quoted forms like "token": "v" also escape, letting the canonical OAuth/API credential assignments persist verbatim into receipts that rounds commit
findings.smallest_fix: widen the pattern to tolerate prefixes and quotes, e.g. re.sub(r"[\w\"']*(api[_-]?key|key|token|secret|password)[\"']?\s*[=:]\s*[\"']?\S+", r"\1=<redacted>", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE), and add a fixture row asserting access_token=supersecretvalue does not survive

findings.failure_path: when a transport failure leaves both the extracted events and stderr empty (SIGKILL/OOM before the CLI writes anything, or the python builders failing soft behind 2>/dev/null), the builder prints nothing and emit_inconclusive drops the key via `if sys.argv[6]`, so the receipt violates the acceptance rule that every transport-failure receipt carries a non-empty transport_diagnostic and reopens the no-evidence hole this change exists to close
findings.smallest_fix: default the empty case before the branch calls, e.g. [ -z "$TRANSPORT_DIAGNOSTIC" ] && TRANSPORT_DIAGNOSTIC="no transport output captured", and add a fixture row for a silent exit-1 failure
